cross_references.notes: Most recent authoritative figures (516 suspected, 131 deaths, 33 confirmed in DRC; 2 confirmed in Uganda) come from the DRC daily health authority bulletin as of 19 May 2026 and are corroborated by Reuters, UN News, and CNBC Africa; earlier WHO DON602 and Africa CDC figures (246 suspected, 8 confirmed, 80 deaths as of 16 May) represent earlier snapshots and are fully consistent with the trend; no material discrepancies between primary sources on current totals.

locations.name: Mongbwalu Health Zone
locations.notes: Considered the origin of the outbreak; a high-traffic gold-mining area where WHO received the first alert on 5 May 2026 regarding an unknown illness with high mortality including four healthcare worker deaths in four days.

locations.name: Rwampara Health Zone
locations.notes: Location of the 13 blood samples analyzed by INRB on 14 May 2026, of which 8 were confirmed Bundibugyo-positive on 15 May, triggering the formal outbreak declaration.

locations.name: Bunia Health Zone
locations.notes: Ituri's provincial capital and initial site of the suspected index case (a healthcare worker who developed symptoms 24 April 2026); hospitals overwhelmed as of 18 May, prompting establishment of field hospitals.

locations.name: Goma
locations.notes: One confirmed case reported 17 May in Goma, a city currently under M23 rebel control on the Rwandan border; Congolese people attempting to cross into Rwanda from Goma were being stopped at the border as of 19 May.

locations.name: Butembo
locations.notes: First two confirmed cases in Butembo, a city of hundreds of thousands in North Kivu, reported 19 May 2026 by INRB director Jean-Jacques Muyembe to Reuters, marking the furthest geographic spread yet within DRC.

locations.name: Kampala
locations.notes: Two imported laboratory-confirmed cases reported 15–16 May 2026 among individuals who travelled from DRC; one death (a 59-year-old Congolese man who died 14 May at Kibuli Muslim Hospital); no local transmission confirmed as of 19 May.

locations.name: Kinshasa
locations.notes: A case initially reported 16 May in an individual returning from Ituri to Kinshasa was confirmed negative for Bundibugyo virus on INRB confirmatory testing; not considered a confirmed case.

timeline.event: Index case — a nurse — presents with fever, hemorrhage, vomiting and malaise at a medical centre in Bunia, Ituri Province, DRC; later dies. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH)

Suspected index case — a nurse at Evangelical Medical Centre, Bunia — develops fever, bleeding, and severe weakness; dies within days. Retrospective investigation suggests she was infected by a patient, implying community transmission was already ongoing.
Earliest known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia — reports symptom onset (fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting); dies at Bunia medical centre. (WHO DON602)
Index case: healthcare worker in Bunia develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and intense malaise — first known suspected case of the outbreak, later dies at a Bunia medical centre.

Suspected index case — a healthcare worker in Bunia, Ituri Province — develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and intense malaise; the individual subsequently dies. This is the earliest known suspected case.
Cluster of unexplained haemorrhagic fever deaths flagged in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, DRC.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown etiology in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths of four health workers within four days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including deaths among healthcare workers; initial GeneXpert tests in Bunia return negative for Zaire Ebola.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality cluster of unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 health-worker deaths within 4 days.
WHO alerted to unknown illness with high mortality in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including four healthcare worker deaths within four days.
MSF receives alerts of increased hemorrhagic fever deaths in Mongbwalu; team deployed finds 55 deaths since early April. (MSF statement)
Rapid-response teams investigate Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 13 blood samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa for advanced analysis. (WHO DON602)
WHO rapid-response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones. (WHO DON602)
WHO/DRC rapid-response teams conduct in-depth field investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara Health Zones; samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa.
WHO rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones; 13 blood samples from Rwampara sent to INRB Kinshasa for analysis.
INRB Kinshasa analyses samples; PCR confirms Orthoebolavirus in 8 of 13 specimens; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). (WHO DON602 / INRB)
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 confirmed Orthoebolavirus-positive by PCR on 15 May. Second Uganda imported case confirmed in Kampala on 16 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara; 8 test positive by PCR for Orthoebolavirus. (WHO DON602)
INRB analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; results released 15 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples; standard Xpert tests in Bunia earlier returned false negatives for all 20 samples tested, as the test detects only Zaire ebolavirus.
Bundibugyo virus confirmed by laboratory (8 of 13 samples positive). First confirmed case detected in Kampala, Uganda.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms imported BVD case — 59-year-old Congolese male who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, on 2026-05-14. (DRC MoH / Uganda MoH / Africa CDC)
Africa CDC activates Incident Management Support Team; convenes urgent cross-border coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, WHO and partners. (Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; INRB confirms 8 positive samples by PCR, genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case — a 59-year-old Congolese man who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala.

INRB genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call. (WHO DON602; Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC; genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV/Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense). Uganda MoH simultaneously declares outbreak following first confirmed imported case in Kampala (Kibuli Muslim Hospital). Africa CDC convenes urgent high-level regional coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan and 130+ global partners.

INRB confirms 8 of 13 samples positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination statement: ~246 suspected cases, 65 deaths.
Second confirmed Kampala case (fatal). Suspected Kinshasa case reported (later retracted).
Second imported confirmed case identified in Kampala with no apparent link to the first; suspected Kinshasa case tests negative on confirmatory INRB PCR and is disconfirmed. (WHO PHEIC / INRB)
WHO Director-General determines the Bundibugyo outbreak in DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC); does not meet pandemic emergency criteria. (WHO)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Uganda; determination cites 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri plus 2 confirmed cases in Kampala and 4 HCW deaths. Africa CDC holds 130-participant high-level consultative meeting.

Second imported case confirmed in Kampala (unlinked to first). WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC. 246 suspected cases, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri confirmed at this time-point. (WHO PHEIC declaration)

Second unrelated confirmed case reported in Kampala, Uganda. WHO Director-General declares a PHEIC under IHR Article 12 — without convening an Emergency Committee, citing the gravity of the situation. Africa CDC activates its Incident Management Support Team.

WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC (declared without Emergency Committee, a first in WHO history). Second imported case confirmed in Kampala. Kinshasa alert issued; later retracted after confirmatory INRB testing negative.
WHO Director-General declares Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

INRB/AFP confirms Goma case: wife of a Bunia Ebola fatality tested positive after traveling to Goma (North Kivu) while already infected, extending geographic spread beyond Ituri. (INRB via AFP / Al Jazeera)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Bundibugyo virus disease; CDC and US State Dept coordinate medical evacuation to Germany for treatment; 6 additional high-risk contacts also moved to Germany. (CDC / NBC News)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo; US officials coordinate evacuation of seven individuals to Germany for care. CDC confirms Level 2 travel health notice for DRC, Level 1 for Uganda.
WHO Emergency Committee to be convened; WHO Director-General confirms PHEIC declared without prior Emergency Committee recommendation — a first in WHO history, citing extraordinary urgency.
WHO formally announces PHEIC; does not declare pandemic emergency. INRB confirms first case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality. (WHO; INRB via AFP)
US missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia; CDC confirms an American has tested positive. (Serge charity; CDC briefing)

INRB Director Muyembe confirms laboratory-positive case in Goma, North Kivu (M23-held city of >1 million, on Rwandan border). Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. Rwanda closes Goma–Gisenyi border crossings indefinitely. American missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms first US national infected.

First confirmed case in Goma, North Kivu, reported — a woman who travelled from Ituri. Africa CDC raises figures to 336 suspected cases, 88 deaths, 13 confirmed. INRB director Muyembe confirms spread to North Kivu.

American physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms the first US national infected. Six other Americans classified as high-risk exposures; all to be moved to Germany for treatment and monitoring.
Outbreak expands from 3 to 9+ health zones in DRC. New confirmed case in Goma (under M23 rebel control). US CDC enacts enhanced travel screening.
Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); reports ~395 suspected cases and 106 associated deaths across DRC and Uganda. (Africa CDC)

CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening, Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who traveled to DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the prior 21 days; CDC EOC activated. (CDC / DHS)

CDC Situation Summary (most recent official update) reports 11 confirmed cases and 336 suspected cases including 88 deaths in DRC, and 2 confirmed cases including 1 death in Uganda across 9 health zones. (CDC Situation Summary)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths confirmed. US CDC/DHS invoke Title 42, restricting entry of non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in prior 21 days.

Ebola confirmed in Goma, North Kivu (rebel-held M23 city); Rwanda closes Goma-Gisenyi border crossings. Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. DRC Health Minister announces three new Ebola treatment centres opening in Ituri.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3(F) of Africa CDC Statute. 395 suspected cases, 106 associated deaths reported. (Africa CDC PHECS declaration)

CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 travel restrictions; entry restrictions placed on non-US passport holders from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan in previous 21 days. CDC moves 7 Americans (1 confirmed case + 6 high-risk contacts) to Germany for care. (CDC)
CDC current situation page confirms 9 health zones in Ituri Province now affected; EU announces PPE stockpiles ready for deployment and detection kit support to Africa CDC. (CDC; CNN)

Africa CDC formally declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 for at least 30 days restricting entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda or South Sudan within the previous 21 days. US moves 7 people (1 confirmed case, 6 high-risk contacts) from DRC to Germany for treatment/monitoring. US Embassy in Uganda temporarily suspends visa services. DRC Health Minister announces opening of 3 new Ebola treatment centres in affected region. WFP airlifts >5 tonnes of medical supplies to Ituri. OCHA reports 482 suspected cases and ~116 deaths in Ituri province alone.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3, Paragraph F of the Africa CDC Statute. CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening and Title 42 entry restrictions for travellers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan within 21 days. CDC confirms 9 health zones in Ituri affected. US State Department issues Do Not Travel advisory for DRC and South Sudan; Reconsider Travel for Uganda and Rwanda.

OCHA reports 482+ suspected cases since April in Ituri; confirms Goma case; warns hostile environment (insecurity, displacement, hunger) is severely hampering response; >5 tonnes of supplies airlifted to Ituri by WFP.
UN News and NBC report outbreak approaching ~500 suspected cases and 116 associated deaths; case in Beni (North Kivu) also reported; situation remains rapidly evolving.

OCHA and UN partners warn hostile environment in eastern DRC is severely hampering response; nearly 10 million people in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu face crisis-level hunger compounding outbreak risk. ECDC deploys expert to Africa CDC headquarters. Reuters witnesses Congolese nationals turned back at Bukavu-Rwanda border. Outbreak total now exceeds 482 suspected cases across at least 9 health zones per OCHA.

DRC daily health bulletin reports 516 suspected cases, 33 confirmed cases, and 131 deaths — including 26 new deaths in 24 hours. WHO representative Dr Anne Ancia confirms spread to North Kivu (Goma and Butembo). Butembo records first 2 confirmed cases (INRB). WHO technical advisory group convenes to assess vaccine options, including Ervebo (Merck) cross-protection potential; WHO notes 2-month timeline before any vaccine could be deployed.

alerts.title: WHO PHEIC declared — Bundibugyo Ebola, DRC & Uganda
alerts.body: On 16 May 2026, WHO Director-General declared the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) — the ninth ever — without convening an Emergency Committee, the first time this has occurred. The outbreak does not meet the criteria of a pandemic emergency but WHO warns the true scale is likely 'much larger than currently detected.'

alerts.title: Africa CDC declares PHECS — 18 May 2026
alerts.body: Africa CDC declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 18 May 2026, empowering continental coordination and rapid resource mobilisation. As of that declaration, approximately 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths had been reported in DRC and Uganda.

alerts.title: Spread to North Kivu confirmed: Goma and Butembo
alerts.body: WHO confirmed cases in both Goma (1 confirmed, 17 May) and Butembo (2 confirmed, 19 May) in North Kivu Province. Goma is under M23 rebel control and borders Rwanda; Butembo is a major commercial hub. Rwanda has closed the border at Goma to DRC crossings.

alerts.title: No approved vaccine or therapeutic for Bundibugyo
alerts.body: WHO, CDC, and Africa CDC confirm there are no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics for Bundibugyo virus. The only approved Ebola vaccines (Merck Ervebo, J&J Zabdeno/Mvabea) target Zaire ebolavirus and are explicitly noted as not effective for this outbreak. A WHO technical advisory group met 19 May to assess options; deployment of any candidate is at least 2 months away.

alerts.title: US Title 42 entry restrictions: DRC, Uganda, South Sudan
alerts.body: On 18 May 2026, CDC and DHS invoked Title 42 to restrict entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days. US State Department issued Do Not Travel advisories for DRC and South Sudan and Reconsider Travel for Uganda and Rwanda.

alerts.title: First American tests positive — Dr. Peter Stafford, Bunia
alerts.body: Dr. Peter Stafford, a Christian missionary physician working in Bunia, DRC, tested positive for Bundibugyo virus on 17 May. He and six other high-risk American contacts are being evacuated to Germany for treatment and monitoring; no cases of Ebola have been confirmed in the United States.

alerts.title: Diagnostic delay of ~3 weeks due to false-negative Xpert tests
alerts.body: Standard Ebola Xpert field tests returned false negatives for 20 initial samples because the assay detects only Zaire ebolavirus. Bundibugyo virus's ~30% genetic divergence caused a 3-week diagnostic delay from the suspected index case (24 April) to confirmation (15 May), allowing significant undetected spread.

alerts.title: Uganda border restrictions at Ishasha-Kyeshero crossing
alerts.body: Ugandan authorities began restricting movement at the Ishasha-Kyeshero DRC-Uganda border crossing as of 19 May to reduce spillover risk; the border is not formally closed but movement is being limited. No local transmission in Uganda has been confirmed.

news.title: Ebola deaths rise to 131 in DRC as outbreak spreads to Butembo, North Kivu
news.summary: DRC's daily health bulletin reports 516 suspected cases, 33 confirmed, and 131 deaths as of 19 May, including 26 new deaths in 24 hours. INRB director Muyembe confirmed the first two cases in Butembo, North Kivu, while the Rwanda border at Goma was closed to DRC crossings.

news.title: WHO rep: over 500 suspected cases, vaccine deployment 'two months away'
news.summary: WHO's DRC representative Dr Anne Ancia told reporters in Geneva on 19 May that there are more than 500 suspected cases and 130 deaths, with only 30 confirmed; she warned a vaccine — with Ervebo (Merck) under review — could take two months to deploy. A WHO technical advisory group met Tuesday to assess options.

news.title: WHO chief 'deeply concerned' by scale and speed of Ebola epidemic
news.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros expressed deep concern on 19 May about the outbreak's rapid spread to North Kivu and beyond; WHO has rushed additional testing kits to eastern DRC and six tonnes of PPE supplies were set to arrive on Tuesday, adding to 12 tonnes already delivered.

news.title: Africa CDC declares Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continental health emergency
news.summary: Africa CDC declared the ongoing Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 18 May 2026, citing approximately 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths in DRC and Uganda. The declaration empowers Africa CDC to lead and coordinate continental response.

news.title: US invokes Title 42, restricts entry from DRC, Uganda and South Sudan
news.summary: CDC and DHS on 18 May implemented Title 42 entry restrictions barring non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days, for a period of 30 days. The US State Department issued Do Not Travel advisories for DRC and South Sudan and a Reconsider Travel advisory for Uganda and Rwanda.

news.title: American doctor Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo in Bunia
news.summary: CDC confirmed on 18 May that Dr. Peter Stafford, a Christian missionary physician working in Bunia, DRC, tested positive for Bundibugyo virus on 17 May; his wife and six other high-risk American contacts are being evacuated to Germany for monitoring and treatment. No US cases have been reported.

news.title: Ebola outbreak raises questions about diagnostic delay and US funding cuts
news.summary: NPR reports that three-week diagnostic delay — caused by Xpert tests detecting only Zaire ebolavirus — allowed hundreds of cases to accumulate before confirmation; public health experts including former USAID officials linked the delayed detection to cuts at CDC, USAID DRC mission closure, and US withdrawal from WHO.

news.title: Scientists play catch-up to startling Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak
news.summary: Science/AAAS reports that Africa CDC chair Salim Abdool Karim stated he is 'really worried this has spread so far, so quickly,' with 10+ confirmed cases spanning Ituri, Goma, and Kampala. Lack of a licensed vaccine complicates response unlike recent Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks.

news.title: NBC News: First American tests positive as Ebola outbreak deepens
news.summary: NBC News reports 500 suspected cases and 116 deaths by 19 May; no approved vaccines or treatments exist for Bundibugyo virus. Johns Hopkins epidemiologist Dr Geeta Sood notes animal studies show existing Zaire-targeted vaccines provide poor cross-protection for Bundibugyo.

news.title: WHO declares Ebola PHEIC without Emergency Committee — a historic first
news.summary: STAT News reports WHO Director-General Tedros issued the PHEIC declaration on 16 May without first seeking advice from an Emergency Committee, the first time this has occurred in WHO history; WHO confirmed a committee would be convened as quickly as possible. The move reflects the speed and scale of the outbreak.

news.title: Africa CDC calls for urgent regional coordination, flags South Sudan risk
news.summary: Africa CDC convened a high-level regional coordination meeting on 16 May 2026 with DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan health authorities alongside WHO, UNICEF, and the Pandemic Fund, citing mining-related population mobility, insecurity, and IPC gaps in affected health zones.

background.virus: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV); formal species name Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus by ~30% genetic divergence
background.case_fatality_rate_historical: 25–51% (WHO/CDC historical range for BDBV: 25–50%; WHO DON602 cites 30–50%; MSF and Johns Hopkins cite 25–40% for BDBV in current outbreak context)
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces, fomites, or bodies of deceased individuals. Individuals are infectious only when symptomatic. Fruit bats are the suspected zoonotic reservoir.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding; nosebleeds and vomiting blood reported in current outbreak. CDC notes most current DRC cases are aged 20–39 and two-thirds are female.
background.vaccines_therapeutics: No licensed vaccine/therapeutic for BDBV; Ervebo under WHO expert review (2-month deployment timeline if cleared); mRNA and mAb candidates pre-clinical only

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak; led to the discovery and naming of the Bundibugyo strain; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel Orthoebolavirus species.
Second documented Bundibugyo outbreak; contained within months in a remote area; second and last BDBV outbreak prior to 2026.

Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, different species (Zaire ebolavirus), but same geographic zone and containment challenges (insecurity, mobile populations, mistrust); directly relevant precedent for current response difficulties.

past_outbreaks.location: Bulape Health Zone, Kasai Province, DRC (Ebola-Zaire)
past_outbreaks.notes: DRC's 16th Ebola outbreak, declared 4 September 2025 and over 1 December 2025; 53 confirmed, 11 probable cases; immediately preceded the current outbreak.

past_outbreaks.location: Ituri Province (epicentre: Mongbwalu, Rwampara, Bunia), North Kivu Province (Goma, Butembo) — DRC; Kampala — Uganda
past_outbreaks.cfr: ~25% of suspected (true CFR undetermined; BDBV historical range 25–50%)
past_outbreaks.notes: Third and largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded; declared PHEIC by WHO 16 May 2026 and PHECS by Africa CDC 18 May 2026; 9 health zones in Ituri affected; confirmed spread to Goma and Butembo (North Kivu) and 2 imported cases in Kampala, Uganda; no approved vaccine or therapeutic; detection delayed ~3 weeks due to false-negative standard Xpert tests; first American (Dr. Peter Stafford) confirmed infected 17 May.

why_this_matters: This is the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded, with 516+ suspected cases already nearly triple the combined total of the two prior BDBV outbreaks (187 cases), and 131 deaths far exceeding those two outbreaks combined.

No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus; the two licensed Ebola vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus and are explicitly noted by the FDA and WHO as not effective for this outbreak, leaving response entirely dependent on classic public-health containment. A WHO technical advisory group convened 19 May to consider emergency use of Ervebo (Merck) for cross-protection, but deployment is estimated at least two months away.

The outbreak has now spread beyond its Ituri epicentre to Goma and Butembo in North Kivu — Goma, a city of over 1 million, is on the Rwandan border and under M23 rebel control, sharply elevating the risk of cross-border transmission into Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, and beyond; Rwanda has closed the DRC border at Goma.

The outbreak zone is in the heart of an active armed conflict in eastern DRC; M23 rebels control Goma, severely impeding access, contact tracing, and the safe operation of treatment centres; healthcare workers have been attacked and population mobility is extreme.

Standard Ebola Xpert field tests returned false negatives for the first 20 samples because they were designed for Zaire ebolavirus, causing a 3–4 week diagnostic delay; Bundibugyo virus's ~30% genetic divergence from Zaire ebolavirus is a critical gap in current field-diagnostic infrastructure.

Healthcare-worker deaths (at least 4 confirmed) and suspected hospital-acquired transmission indicate critical IPC gaps, with the outbreak amplified through both formal and informal health facilities across Ituri.

A US citizen healthcare worker (Dr. Peter Stafford) has been confirmed infected in Bunia, prompting US Title 42 travel restrictions — barring entry to non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan who have been in those countries within 21 days — and a Do Not Travel advisory for DRC.

Cuts to global public-health funding — including USAID DRC mission closure, reduced CDC capacity, and US withdrawal from WHO — have been directly linked by public-health experts to surveillance failures that allowed this outbreak to accumulate hundreds of cases before detection, with a former CDC official noting it 'does seem weird that we accrued a couple 100 cases of this before CDC got any inkling.'

WHO convened an Emergency Committee after-the-fact (the PHEIC was declared without one, a historic first), and the most advanced vaccine candidate — Ervebo — faces both scientific uncertainty about cross-species effectiveness against BDBV and a ~2-month logistical deployment timeline, meaning containment relies entirely on traditional public-health tools in one of the world's most challenging operational environments.
